accepted before or after the optional count that prints exactly one JSON
object with an integer `widgets` field (default 0), and replace the crash
with a useful stderr failure — no traceback, nonzero exit — for invalid
input including extra positional arguments. One cohesive task owns the code
and the real subprocess CLI tests; no new dependencies.

Anyone running `count.py` with a non-integer argument or extra positionals
today gets an uncaught `ValueError` traceback (exit 1) instead of a usage
message, and there is no machine-readable (`--json`) output for callers that
parse results. Nothing pins the CLI contract: no tests, no documented usage
(README is a one-line heading), so regressions in the only product surface
would ship silently.

The developer/evaluator invoking the `count.py` command line directly and
any script that shells out to it. Single-user fixture scale; technical.

## Summary

`count.py` is a 3-line stdlib CLI that prints `N widgets` for an optional
integer argument, defaults to 0, and dies with an uncaught `ValueError`
traceback on invalid input; it has no tests and no machine-readable output.
This milestone hardens that CLI in place: keep the existing plain output
format, accept a signed integer count (default 0), add a `--json` flag
accepted before or after the optional count that prints exactly one JSON
object with an integer `widgets` field (default 0), and replace the crash
with a useful stderr failure — no traceback, nonzero exit — for invalid
input including extra positional arguments. One cohesive task owns the code
and the real subprocess CLI tests; no new dependencies.

## Problem

Anyone running `count.py` with a non-integer argument or extra positionals
today gets an uncaught `ValueError` traceback (exit 1) instead of a usage
message, and there is no machine-readable (`--json`) output for callers that
parse results. Nothing pins the CLI contract: no tests, no documented usage
(README is a one-line heading), so regressions in the only product surface
would ship silently.

## Users

The developer/evaluator invoking the `count.py` command line directly and
any script that shells out to it. Single-user fixture scale; technical.

4. `--json` before or after the optional count is equivalent:

5. Invalid input — non-integer count or extra positional arguments — fails
